policy: in-flight (running) jobs always finish and lead run_now ordered by remaining estimate ascending (ties by id); queued jobs requeue in ORIGINAL queue order, except idempotent jobs whose deadline is inside the inclusive drain window (now <= deadline <= now + window) run now after the in-flight jobs, ordered by deadline then id; queued jobs with deadline < now are dropped entirely (even idempotent ones) and recorded in the third returned list, original order
bug_report: Rolling restarts take forever - workers sit on long jobs while short ones wait - and a customer's scheduled export ran twice right after a deploy; separately, ops found six-week-old jobs resurrected and executing after last week's restart. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py. Fix drain_order so the shutdown plan matches the drain policy, without breaking existing behaviour.
non_guessable: decision lives in git history (a documented commit), broken by a misleading 'perf' regression commit; git log/blame is the shortcut
decision_subject: fix: drain_order shutdown plan - in-flight ordering, idempotent carve-out, expired-deadline drops
decision_rationale: Every symptom from the last restart wave traced to drain_order treating a drain as an id-sorted requeue. The plan is three rules. In-flight jobs (state == 'running') always finish and lead run_now ordered by remaining estimate ascending - shortest first, ties by id - because finishing short work first frees workers fastest and that's what bounds the restart. Queued jobs are requeued, with one carve-out: a queued job marked idempotent whose deadline falls inside the drain window (now <= deadline <= now + window) runs now, after the in-flight jobs, ordered by deadline then id - idempotent-only because rerunning anything else after the requeue double-fires it, which is exactly the duplicated-export incident. Everything else requeues in its ORIGINAL queue order (no re-sorting - the queue order is a fairness promise), except that a queued job whose deadline is already exceeded (deadline < now) is dropped entirely and recorded in the returned dropped list, original order - requeuing expired work is how ancient jobs got resurrected after last week's restart.
